stages.a: The bag is folded over the block and cut.
stages.v: Handled like lion's mane: fold the bag over and cut an X, a straight slit or an H.

stages.a: A short, thick column grows out of the cut.
stages.v: It grows out as a column, then branches. Slow to start, then it combs out fast.

stages.a: The column splits again and again, like Romanesco cauliflower.
stages.v: The branching phase ("fractalization") lasts about 5-7 days. It browns in too much air and goes popcorny in stagnant air.

stages.a: A dense, cloud-like head with teeth hanging under every branch.
stages.v: Pick at the end of the branching phase, when the branching has finished. It prefers 19-21 °C.

stages.a: The branches droop and the head goes soft.
stages.v: Mature fruit droops and turns spongy and cauliflower-like, so pick before that.

labels.a: The cut in the folded bag.
labels.v: An X, a straight slit or an H.

labels.a: The thick column it grows from.
labels.v: Comb tooth holds on to the cut with a big trunk.
It branches repeatedly like Romanesco cauliflower.

labels.a: Short teeth hang in rows under the branches.
labels.v: Spinier and less "tentacled" than lion's mane.
Mature fruit droops: pick before that.

labels.a: The teeth swell and the head goes soft.
